newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower in light OTC trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower in light OTC trade.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were expected to open marginally lower Tuesday as moderate weather and a lighter end-of-the-month physical market tempered demand, industry sources said.
June over-the-counter ranged from $2.05 to $2.07 in light trade following Monday's settlement to the downside at $2.081 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, June last traded 0.1 cent higher at $2.082 after reaching a high of $2.094 earlier.
"The call is one to two lower, but it's quiet with May cash done and warm weather everywhere," one trader said.

After breaking through $2.07, June delivery's next support was pegged by technical traders at $2.03 and then along the short-term up trendline at $2.00. Resistance was seen at $2.24 and then at $2.33.

In Monday's cash market, May Gulf Coast gas was talked about five cents lower at $2.04-09. May Midcon prices slipped a few cents to the low-to-mid $1.90s. New York city gate gas for May also was modestly lower around $2.40.

Near-normal temperatures are expected to continue this week throughout most of the upper Midwest and Northeast, with cooler air forecast to reach the southern plains and Texas by the latter part of the week.
